item.title: Former general election candidate sets sights on Leinster House
item.description: A former general election candidate has set his sights on a place in Leinster House in the future. West Sligo-based councillor Michael Clarke contested the 2024 general election in Sligo-Leitrim. Representing Independent Ireland, he picked up almost 6 thousand first preference votes. item.title: Funding sought for potential Longford music museum
item.description: Calls have been made for Longford County Council to seek funding for a Museum of Music Ireland in the former Providers building on Lower Main Street. The project could be supported by a new €7.5 million Towns and Cities Regeneration Investment Fund, which opens for applications this week. The museum would be an immersive heritage attraction celebrating Longford's strong links to Irish country music. item.title: Poultry farmers urged to remain vigilant amid bird flu outbreaks
item.description: Poultry farmers across the Shannonside region are being urged to remain vigilant following reports of a suspected bird flu outbreak at a pheasant breeding premises in Co Tyrone. It is the latest in a series of outbreaks across the country. Producers are being reminded to remain alert and ensure the highest standards of biosecurity are in place across all poultry, backyard and game bird operations. item.title: Major extension announced for Carrick-on-Shannon Community School
item.description: A major extension has been announced for Carrick-on-Shannon's Community School. There will be eight new general classes and the refurbishment of the music room to provide a general classroom, 2 SET rooms, 2 science labs, 1 science prep area, 1 art room & 1 home economics room. item.title: Local businesses not responsible for fuel spikes- Carrigy
item.description: A local TD says those who work in local fuel depots shouldn't be subjected to abuse over rising fuel costs. Fine Gael's Micheál Carrigy was speaking as fuel prices hit €2 per litre in some areas today. Local Enterprise Minister Peter Burke had earlier stated that the abuse is unacceptable. item.description: The Enterprise Minister has labelled the abuse experienced by forecourt workers following fuel price hikes as "unacceptable". Peter Burke made the comments after meeting with forecourt operators and home heating suppliers about dramatic rises in fuel costs since the US and Israel began bombing Iran. The Government have confirmed that the CCPC is to investigate claims of price gouging over fuel. item.title: Roscommon included scrambler in bike statistics
item.description: New research from the Road Safety Authority is highlighting the risks linked to scrambler bikes on Irish roads - with over 50 people killed or seriously injured in recent years. The RSA review of Garda collision data shows that three people died and more than fifty others were seriously injured in scrambler-related crashes between 2021 and 2025. item.title: Local councils allocated energy efficiency funding
item.description: County Councils in the Shannonside region have been allocated over €6 million in funding under the Energy Efficiency Retrofit Programme. It is part of a pot of €140 million that is on the way to local authorities under the scheme. Locally, Roscommon County Council is to receive €3.7 million, Longford €2.6 million while €700,000 is on the way to Leitrim County Council.
